title: Runtime performance remediation from manual perf smoke evidence
references: Current manual evidence: npm run perf:browser -- --cycles 3 reports roughly +1.91 MB heap and no extra network transfer during a normal GP loop; npm run perf:replay -- --cycles 3 reports roughly +5.33 MB heap, +209 DOM nodes, and +135 event listeners while staying on the replay screen and toggling replay controls.
Current manual evidence: perf:compare marks replay stress as worse than the normal GP loop, so the first runtime optimization target is replay UI retention rather than API or network.

Current manual evidence: perf:bundle reports apps/web/dist around 14.29 MB, with images around 10.66 MB and JS around 2.4 MB. Largest files include assets/crl/finish-flag.png around 1393 KB, the app chunk around 489 KB, stand.png around 469 KB, and circuit-routes around 455 KB.

Current manual evidence: perf:api -- --cycles 20 reports average race resolution around 3.1 ms, p95 around 8.1-8.9 ms, average result JSON around 111.85 KB, heap delta after GC around 0.82 MB, and RSS delta around 14-15 MB. API CPU is not the first bottleneck.

Code scan: replay-related hooks with timers/animation/listeners live in ReplayView.tsx, useReplayClock.ts, ReplayStageOverlay.tsx, and CircuitMap.tsx. PWA listeners in app/pwa.ts are long-lived by design and should not be treated as replay leaks without evidence.

needs: Reduce retained browser memory, DOM nodes, and event listeners during replay usage, based on the new manual perf smoke evidence.
Keep replay behavior, controls, camera/focus modes, timeline, stage overlays, and report/replay navigation unchanged for players.
Clean up obviously shipped build-output hygiene issues if confirmed by perf:bundle, especially accidental non-runtime artifacts in apps/web/dist.
Reduce the most expensive image payloads only where measurement shows meaningful savings and the UI does not visually regress.
Keep API/simulation optimization as a measured watchpoint rather than a first implementation target unless new evidence contradicts the current perf:api results.
Use the manual perf tools for before/after evidence; do not add CI gates or blocking perf budgets yet.
context: This request follows the manual profiling tool pass. The app now has npm run perf:browser, perf:replay, perf:compare, perf:bundle, and perf:api. These tools are intentionally manual and must remain outside CI for this request.

The strongest signal is replay retention: replay stress grows heap, DOM nodes, and listeners more than the normal GP loop while network transfer stays flat. Inspect cleanup and retention in ReplayView, useReplayClock, ReplayStageOverlay, and CircuitMap first.

Likely replay remediation areas: requestAnimationFrame cancellation, setTimeout cleanup, speed/focus menu listeners, SVG connector/marker retention, animation/camera state held after replay restart or control toggles, and duplicate DOM generated by repeated replay interactions.

Do not weaken replay UX to improve metrics. The replay must still render map, cars, director beats, start/finish presentation, weather/timeline, focus driver, speed controls, restart, pause/play, and Back to stand.

Bundle evidence is secondary but actionable. perf:bundle reports image weight dominates. Also verify whether apps/web/dist contains non-runtime artifacts (for example tsbuildinfo, test JS, maps, or source TS) because those should not ship if served by production.

The existing draft request req_124 covers eager bundle trimming and script/document boundaries. Avoid duplicating req_124; this corpus should either consume its findings as context or leave broad code-splitting to that request. This request may fix dist hygiene if it is small and directly confirmed.

API evidence does not justify first-pass optimization: race simulation is low milliseconds and no database path is involved in perf:api. Preserve the API payload watchpoint, especially replayTrace/result JSON size, but do not spend effort there before replay retention.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A before/after perf:replay run with at least 10 cycles shows reduced retained heap, DOM node, and/or listener growth versus the recorded baseline, and perf:compare marks the after run as better or stable for the targeted metrics.

AC2: Replay controls and flows remain functionally intact: pause/play, restart, speed selection, focus driver, map/cars, weather/timeline, race director overlays, report access, and Back to stand still work.
AC3: The implementation includes the smallest necessary cleanup fixes for replay timers/listeners/animation state; any persistent growth that remains is documented with a clear suspected owner.

AC4: perf:bundle is rerun after changes. If non-runtime artifacts are present in apps/web/dist, they are removed from the production output or explicitly documented if they are local-only artifacts not served in production.
AC5: At least the largest image payloads are reviewed. Any converted/resized asset has before/after size evidence and no broken image requests in representative app flows.
AC6: API/simulation perf remains a watchpoint only unless perf:api regresses; no API contract or race result payload shape changes without separate product approval.

AC7: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test, npm run build, npm run test:e2e -- --project=chromium, npm run perf:replay -- --cycles 10, npm run perf:bundle, and npm run logics:validate pass or have documented non-blocking perf evidence where applicable.

product.title: Runtime Performance Remediation Product Brief
product.overview: Manual performance smoke tests show CR League's replay screen retains more heap, DOM nodes, and browser listeners than the normal GP loop, while network and API CPU are not currently the main bottlenecks. This brief prioritizes replay runtime cleanup, then lightweight build-output and asset hygiene, using the new manual perf tools for before/after proof without introducing CI perf gates.
goals: Reduce replay runtime growth without changing player-facing replay behavior.
Use perf:replay and perf:compare as the primary evidence loop.
Confirm production build output does not contain accidental non-runtime artifacts.
Review the largest shipped images for cheap byte reductions with visual safety.
Keep API simulation performance measured but out of the first optimization path.
non_goals: Do not add CI perf budgets, Lighthouse gates, dashboards, or new profiling dependencies.
Do not redesign replay, map, race report, championship, garage, or navigation UX.
Do not remove replay features to improve metrics.
Do not change API contracts, replayTrace/result payload shape, or simulation behavior in this pass.
Do not duplicate broad code-splitting work already covered by req_124 unless a tiny dist-hygiene fix is directly required.

backlog_items.title: Reduce replay runtime retention in timers, listeners, and SVG state
problem: perf:replay -- --cycles 3 shows materially more retained heap, DOM nodes, and listeners than the normal GP loop.
Replay has several likely retention points: requestAnimationFrame loops, setTimeout queues, connector SVG measurement, replay camera/focus state, speed menu state, and restart/pause interactions.
The player-facing replay experience is central to CR League, so optimization must preserve behavior rather than remove features.
scope_in: Run npm run perf:replay -- --cycles 10 and record a before baseline JSON/Markdown.

Inspect ReplayView.tsx, replay/useReplayClock.ts, replay/ReplayStageOverlay.tsx, and CircuitMap.tsx for missing cleanup, stale closures, repeated listener/timer setup, or retained DOM-producing state.
Patch the smallest shared cleanup points: cancel animation frames, clear timers, bound transient replay state on restart/exit, and avoid accumulating SVG/overlay nodes or event listeners.
Rerun perf:replay -- --cycles 10 and perf:compare against the before JSON.
Run the private-league Chromium e2e flow to confirm replay controls and navigation still work.
scope_out: Replay redesign, animation removal, or disabling focus/speed/restart features.
Changing simulation trace generation or race result schema.
PWA install/update listener work unless the perf tools prove it is part of replay growth.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: After-run perf:replay has lower retained heap, DOM node, and/or listener growth than the before baseline, or any remaining growth is explained with evidence.
AC2: perf:compare reports better or stable for the targeted replay metrics.
AC3: Replay pause/play, restart, speed selection, focus driver, Back to stand, and report access still work in e2e/manual checks.
AC4: typecheck, lint, tests, build, Chromium e2e, and logics validation pass.

backlog_items.title: Verify production dist hygiene and remove accidental shipped artifacts
problem: perf:bundle reports apps/web/dist contains categories such as tsbuildinfo, source maps, TS, and test JS in the local dist scan.
Some entries may be local build residue or copied artifacts rather than production-served files; this must be verified before changing build config.
Broad eager bundle splitting is already covered by req_124, so this item should stay focused on accidental output hygiene.
scope_in: Run a clean production build from a clean dist directory and rerun npm run perf:bundle.
Identify whether any test JS, TS source, source maps, or tsbuildinfo files are actually inside apps/web/dist after the clean build.
If accidental artifacts are present, fix the smallest build/config issue that emits them or clean them from production output.
Document if the earlier artifacts were only stale local residue and not reproducible.
scope_out: Large code-splitting work already tracked by req_124.
Changing TypeScript project architecture beyond what is needed to stop accidental output.
Adding a new bundle analyzer dependency.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A clean-build perf:bundle report is captured.
AC2: No accidental test/source/tsbuildinfo files remain in production dist, or the report documents that they were not reproducible.
AC3: npm run build and npm run perf:bundle pass after the cleanup.

backlog_items.title: Review largest image payloads for cheap measured reductions
problem: perf:bundle shows images dominate dist size: roughly 10.66 MB out of 14.29 MB.
The largest current image is finish-flag.png around 1393 KB, followed by other large gameplay/UI artwork.
Blind conversion can duplicate assets or degrade visuals, so this must be measurement-led and narrow.
scope_in: Review the top image payloads from perf:bundle and identify obvious candidates for WebP conversion, resizing, or removal if unused.
For each changed asset, record before/after file size and verify representative flows do not show broken images.
Prefer existing asset patterns and static files; do not add a permanent image pipeline dependency.
scope_out: Regenerating artwork content or redesigning screens.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: At least the largest image payloads are reviewed with recorded keep/change rationale.
AC2: Any changed asset has before/after size evidence and no broken image requests in representative app flows.
AC3: perf:bundle shows the updated size after changes.

backlog_items.title: Keep API simulation performance as a measured watchpoint
problem: perf:api currently shows low-millisecond simulation times, so API CPU is not the first bottleneck.
The average race result JSON is around 111.85 KB, which may matter later if replay payload/network evidence changes.
Premature API contract changes would risk gameplay and replay compatibility.
scope_in: Rerun npm run perf:api -- --cycles 100 after replay/build work to ensure no regression.
Record duration and JSON-size evidence in the task closeout.
Open a separate request only if API duration, memory, or payload size becomes a measured problem.
scope_out: Changing API contracts or replayTrace/result payload shape.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: perf:api evidence is captured after the frontend performance changes.
AC2: No API contract or simulation behavior changes are made in this pass.
AC3: Any newly discovered API concern is documented as a follow-up instead of hidden inside replay cleanup.

orchestration_task.title: Orchestrate runtime performance remediation
plan: Run the manual perf baselines first: perf:replay -- --cycles 10, perf:browser -- --cycles 10 if needed, perf:bundle, and perf:api -- --cycles 100. Save reports under reports/perf but do not version generated reports unless explicitly requested.
Start with replay retention. Inspect ReplayView, useReplayClock, ReplayStageOverlay, and CircuitMap for missing cleanup and retained animation/listener/SVG state. Patch the smallest cleanup points.
Rerun perf:replay and perf:compare against the baseline. Keep iterating only while changes are clearly grounded in the metrics.
Verify replay behavior through the private league Chromium e2e flow and targeted manual checks for pause/play, restart, speed, focus, report access, and Back to stand.
Run a clean production build and perf:bundle. Fix accidental dist artifacts if reproduced; otherwise document that the earlier artifact signal was stale local residue.
Review the largest image payloads, changing only assets with meaningful measured savings and no broken visual flows.
Rerun perf:api as a watchpoint and avoid API/payload contract changes unless new evidence makes them necessary.
Run typecheck, lint, tests, build, Chromium e2e, logics validation, and record before/after evidence in the task closeout.
